== Biography ==

The Tin Woodman, also known as Nick Chopper and holding the title of Emperor, is a longtime companion of Dorothy and the Wizard, encountered on their travels through Oz. Dorothy recalls that she and the Scarecrow once found him rusted still in the woods, and after oiling his joints, he accompanied them to visit the Wizard at the Emerald City. He maintains a tin castle in the Winkie Country, where travelers such as Dorothy, Aunt Em, Uncle Henry, and the Wizard have lunched with him and toured his tin gardens and fish pond.

The Tin Woodman speaks with insight about his fellow companion the Scarecrow, observing that the Scarecrow cannot be contented with city life despite its beauty, noting that the Scarecrow was originally a farmer who passed his early life in a cornfield meant to frighten away crows.

According to Dorothy's account, the Emperor is described as kind-hearted. He is also said to have offered to arm his Winkies and march to Ozma's assistance, which suggests an allied relationship with her, though this connection is not stated outright as established fact. His account of the Nome King digging a tunnel under the desert to invade Oz alongside the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms is presented from his own subjective telling of what Ozma saw in her Magic Picture, rather than as directly witnessed fact.

== Narrative role ==

Before Tin Woodman himself appears, the plan to visit him is already in motion: the traveling group, resting for the night, decides to continue their journey the next day and intends to call on Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Scarecrow, after first passing through the Rigmaroles and the Flutterbudgets.

The visit itself becomes a central episode of the journey when the travelers finally reach Winkie Country and lunch with Tin Woodman — referred to as the Emperor — at his tin castle, where he receives them and shows them through his tin gardens and his fish pond.

During this stay, Tin Woodman, also known as Nick Chopper, passes along grave news: he reveals that Ozma has seen in her Magic Picture that [[Nome King]] has dug a tunnel under the desert in order to invade Oz, in league with Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms.

== Personality ==

Le Tin Woodman fait preuve de finesse dans son jugement des autres : lorsqu'il constate que leur cher Scarecrow ne semble pas pouvoir se satisfaire de la vie citadine, aussi belle que soit cette existence, il rattache ce mécontentement à l'origine du Scarecrow — né fermier, ayant passé sa jeunesse dans un champ de maïs à effrayer les corbeaux — plutôt qu'à un défaut du cadre urbain lui-même. Cette manière de chercher la cause profonde d'un état d'esprit plutôt que de s'arrêter aux apparences suggère un tempérament réfléchi et perspicace.

Il est par ailleurs décrit par un tiers comme quelqu'un de très bienveillant, une appréciation qui, provenant d'une relation de simple connaissance plutôt que d'un lien étroit, reste à prendre avec prudence mais dessine l'image d'un personnage perçu comme doux dans ses rapports avec autrui.

== Appearance ==

The Tin Woodman is built entirely of tin, with jointed limbs prone to rusting. On one occasion he was found in the woods "rusted still," frozen in place until Dorothy and the Scarecrow oiled his joints and got them "good and slippery" again, restoring his movement.

== Powers ==

The Tin Woodman's body is made entirely of tin, a construction that leaves him prone to rust and reliant on oiling to stay mobile. Dorothy recalls finding him in the woods "rusted still," after which she and the Scarecrow "oiled his joints an' got 'em good and slippery," restoring his movement. This need for regular oiling to remain functional marks his tin form as fundamentally unlike an ordinary body.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Ozma]]''' — ally. He offers to arm all his Winkies and march to Ozma's assistance, which suggests a supportive, allied bond between them.

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. He speaks of her as "my little friend Dorothy," suggesting a warm, protective friendship.

'''[[Wizard]]''' — acquaintance. He is described as "very kind-hearted," a remark that could indicate a cordial, if not close, acquaintance with the Wizard.

'''[[Nome King]]''' — enemy. It is suggested that the Nome King has been harboring wicked thoughts of revenge against him since an earlier defeat, hinting at a lasting antagonism between them.

'''[[Aunt Em]]''' — acquaintance. Their connection is only faintly suggested by context and remains uncertain.

== Trivia ==

* Dorothy recalls finding the Tin Woodman rusted stiff in the woods along with the Scarecrow, and oiling his joints until they moved freely again.
* After being freed, he traveled with Dorothy and the Scarecrow to visit the Wizard at the Emerald City.
